description_full: ZTO Express (Cayman) Inc. provides express delivery and other value-added logistics services in the People's Republic of China. It also offers less-than-truckload (LTL) logistics services; integrated logistics solutions for warehousing, distribution, and transportation; and freight forwarding services. The company was founded in 2002 and is headquartered in Shanghai, the People's Republic of China.
ceo_bio: Mr. Meisong  Lai | Founder, Chairman & CEO | Age 54 | Compensation: $249,768 (FY2025)
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 23K people. Revenue per employee of $308K ranks in the below the sector median among Industrials peers, improving at 19%/yr — growing workforce leverage. Each employee generates $42K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $1K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 1× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity).
financial_summary: ZTO Express (Cayman) Inc. is a large-cap industrials business with a $15.5B market cap on $7.4B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +9% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 22% against a 8% cost of capital — a 14-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 30%.

The business throws off $1.0B in free cash flow — roughly 14 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.32× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 42× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 4.8% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 3.0% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 1.9× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

mkt: The shares have drifted higher, up 6% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 14% over the last three months.

prof: ROIC of 22% clears the cost of capital of 8.2% by 14pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have been steady (CV 0.26).

Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 7/9 and cash conversion of 1.32x.

hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $539.0M.

growth: Revenue has compounded at 9.1% over 3 years and 13.3% over 5 years, so growth is decelerating.
At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 21.9% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Capex runs 1.5x depreciation (10.6% of sales), so it is building capacity for future growth.
Its Rule of 40 score is 27, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 8.6% on average.
own: Insiders own a modest 3.0%, and institutions hold 12%.
It returns 4.8% a year to shareholders (1.2% in buybacks and 3.3% in dividends).

people: With about 23,888 employees, each generates about $308K of revenue, 0.8x the Industrials median, and productivity has risen 18.6% a year.
That works out to $42K of free cash flow per employee.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
